obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived exact target relation; finite checks are not a semantic proof
obernants.assumptions: Validated labels, documented cap and deterministic integer operations
obernants.domain: Documented capped API domain, or explicitly bounded deterministic test universe
obernants.observation_scope: Typed errors, canonical graph/code outputs and named assertions
obernants.operator: U contains labeled edge lists or words, explicit n, and candidate Result values. Wrong lengths/labels, loops, reversed duplicates, or cyclic n-1 edge lists cannot yield Ok. For valid trees, code from a nonminimum current leaf is excluded; decode outputs with wrong degrees, noncanonical edge order, cycles or missing connectivity are excluded.

obernants.operator: For n>=2 fixed n, the valid code identifies one undirected labeled tree; encoding forgets edge order and endpoint orientation, so its concrete edge-list fiber contains all permutations and orientations of that tree. Decode with fixed n has one compatible word. Without n, [] also represents the distinct n=0,1,2 conventions; omitting n loses that distinction.

obernants.operator: For n>=2, fixing just decoded degree vector d admits every word of length n-2 with exactly d(v)-1 occurrences of v; occurrence order is lost by the degree observation. Different such words may encode different trees. Full code retains this order and restores the unique labeled edge set.

obernants.operator: encode first rejects n>MAX_VERTICES, then edges.len()!=n.saturating_sub(1), then processes edges in order: u label, v label, self-loop, normalized duplicate, DSU cycle. A reversed repeat reports RepeatedEdge before the cycle check; a first cycle reports NotTree before inspecting later edges. With n-1 distinct loopless edges, acyclicity implies connectedness for n>0. decode checks cap then length then labels. Thus a wrong-length word with an invalid symbol yields WrongLength. n=0/1 accept only empty edge lists and words.

obernants.operator: For fixed n>=2, decode(encode(n,E)) equals the sorted set of normalized edges {(min(u,v),max(u,v))}; it need not equal E as an ordered oriented list. encode(decode(n,C))=C for every valid word. At each elimination the heap chooses the smallest live degree-one label, so the star/path fixture [(4,0),(4,1),(4,2),(4,3),(3,5)] yields [4,4,4,3]. The degree fiber alone loses this temporal order: for n=4 codes [0,1] and [1,0] have the same degrees [2,2,1,1] but different decoded trees.
